examples.en: The lights suddenly went out and the room turned pitch dark.

examples.ko: 할머니 어릴 때는 시골에 전깃불이 없었대요.
examples.en: They say there was no electric light in the countryside when Grandma was little.

examples.ko: 잠깐 나갈 거니까 전깃불을 끄지 마세요.
examples.en: I'm only stepping out for a moment, so please don't turn off the light.

examples.ko: 전깃불 아래에서 책을 읽으면 눈이 피곤해요.
examples.en: Reading under electric light makes my eyes tired.
Electricity only came to our village last year.
Electric light is much brighter than candlelight, so it's more convenient.

explain: '불'이나 '전등'보다 전기로 켜는 불이라는 느낌이 있어서, 촛불이나 등잔불과 비교하는 옛날이야기에 잘 어울려요. '전깃불이 나가다'는 정전됐을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Compared with '불' or '전등', it carries the feeling of a light turned on by electricity, so it fits old stories that contrast it with candles or oil lamps. '전깃불이 나가다' is what you say when the power goes out.

examples.en: My older sister studied nursing at a junior college.

examples.ko: 전문대는 보통 이 년이나 삼 년 만에 졸업해요.
examples.en: You usually graduate from a junior college in two or three years.
I graduated from junior college and went straight into a company.
There is one junior college in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 전문대 입학 시험을 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger brother is preparing for a junior college entrance exam.

examples.ko: 전문대와 대학교 중에서 어디로 갈지 고민이에요.
examples.en: I'm torn between a junior college and a university.

explain: 4년제 '대학교'와 짝으로 자주 말하고, 보통 과정이 더 짧고 직업 기술을 배우는 쪽이에요. 정식 이름은 '전문대학'이지만 말할 때는 대부분 '전문대'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is often paired with the four-year '대학교', and its programs are usually shorter and focused on job skills. The formal name is '전문대학', but in speech people mostly say '전문대'.

examples.en: The electric pole fell backward because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 전봇대 옆에 쓰레기를 버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not throw trash next to the electric pole.
I bumped my head on an electric pole while walking.
Flyers are plastered on every electric pole.
The meeting spot is in front of the blue electric pole.
Please park the car so it avoids the electric pole.

explain: '전신주'라는 말도 있지만 말할 때는 '전봇대'가 더 편하고 흔한 느낌이에요. 약속 장소를 알려 줄 때 '파란 전봇대 앞'처럼 길 표시로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: There is also the word '전신주', but '전봇대' feels more casual and natural in speech. People also use it as a landmark when giving directions, like '파란 전봇대 앞'.

examples.en: The jeonse deposit went up, so I have to move.
I took out a bank loan to put together the jeonse deposit.
My parents chipped in a little toward the jeonse deposit.
You get the jeonse deposit back when the contract ends.

examples.ko: 전셋돈 때문에 두 사람이 자주 싸워요.
examples.en: The two of them often argue over the jeonse deposit.
About how much is the jeonse deposit in this neighborhood?

explain: '전세금'과 같은 뜻으로 편하게 말할 때 써요. 월세처럼 매달 내는 돈이 아니라 집주인에게 맡겨 두었다가 나중에 돌려받는 큰돈이라서, 대출이나 이사 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means the same as '전세금' and sounds more casual. Unlike monthly rent, it is a large sum left with the landlord and returned later, so it comes up often in talk about loans and moving.

examples.en: The place I live in now is a jeonse home.
I went to a real estate office to find a good jeonse home.
My jeonse contract ends next month.
We began our married life in a small jeonse home.

examples.ko: 전셋집은 마음대로 벽에 못을 박기 어려워요.
examples.en: In a jeonse home it's hard to hammer nails into the wall as you like.
I heard a jeonse home became available near the office.

explain: '월세방'처럼 매달 월세를 내는 집과 구분할 때, 또 '내 집'과 구분할 때 써요. 전세는 한국에서 쓰는 독특한 집 계약 방식이라서 번역보다 그대로 '전세'로 기억하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: Use it to set a home apart from a '월세방' where you pay monthly rent, or from a home you own ('내 집'). Jeonse is a housing contract style particular to Korea, so it is better to remember it as 'jeonse' than as a translation.

examples.ko: 아버지가 생일 선물로 전자시계를 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father bought me a digital watch as a birthday present.

examples.ko: 이 전자시계는 알람도 맞출 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can set an alarm on this digital watch too.
The digital watch stopped, so I changed the battery.
The date also shows on the digital watch screen.

examples.ko: 수영할 때 찰 전자시계를 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a digital watch to wear when I swim.
I set the time with the digital watch.

explain: 바늘이 있는 '아날로그 시계'와 달리 숫자로 시간을 보여 주는 시계를 말해요. '디지털시계'라고도 하는데, 전자시계는 건전지나 알람 같은 기능 이야기와 같이 나오는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is the clock that shows time in numbers, as opposed to an analog clock with hands. People also say '디지털시계', and '전자시계' often comes up when talking about batteries or alarm features.

examples.en: I forgot the phone number, so I looked through the phone directory.
In the old days every house had a thick phone directory.
I looked up the hospital's number in the phone directory.
The shop's number wasn't in the phone directory.

examples.ko: 스마트폰 전화번호부에 저장된 사람이 삼백 명이나 돼요.
examples.en: There are as many as three hundred people saved in my smartphone's phone book.
I threw away the old phone directory when I moved.

explain: 종이로 된 두꺼운 책을 떠올리게 하지만, 스마트폰 안의 연락처 목록을 가리킬 때도 써요. 폰 이야기에서는 '연락처'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: It brings to mind a thick paper book, but it can also refer to the contact list inside a smartphone. When talking about phones, people often say '연락처' too.

examples.ko: 동생은 하루 종일 전화통을 붙잡고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is glued to the phone all day long.
The phone rang, so I ran over quickly.
My father spoke loudly into the phone.

examples.ko: 낡은 전화통은 이제 박물관에서나 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only see old telephone sets in museums now.
My friend does nothing but chat away on the phone.

examples.ko: 전화통 앞에서 한참 망설이다가 전화를 걸었어요.
examples.en: I hesitated in front of the phone for a long time before making the call.

explain: '전화기'보다 말투가 편하고 옛날 전화기 느낌이 있어요. '전화통을 붙잡고 있다'처럼 오랫동안 통화하는 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 신제품이 나온 뒤로 고객센터 전화통에 불이 났어요.
phrases.en: The customer center's phones have been ringing off the hook since the new product came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전화가 쉴 새 없이 걸려 오거나 걸 때 쓰는 말이에요. 실제로 불이 나는 게 아니라 아주 바쁘다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when calls keep coming in (or going out) without a break. There is no real fire; it is a figure of speech for being extremely busy with calls.

explain_en: It sounds more casual than '전화기' and has an old-fashioned telephone feel. It is often used in phrases like '전화통을 붙잡고 있다' to describe someone on a long call.

examples.en: After failing the exam, a sense of despair washed over me.

examples.ko: 그는 깊은 절망감에 빠져 아무것도 못 했어요.
examples.en: He fell into deep despair and couldn't do anything.
I couldn't overcome the despair of being alone.

examples.ko: 절망감 속에서도 친구의 말 한마디가 힘이 됐어요.
examples.en: Even in despair, a single word from a friend gave me strength.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 절망감과 희망을 함께 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This movie shows both despair and hope.

examples.ko: 계속된 실패로 절망감은 점점 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: The despair grew bigger and bigger because of repeated failures.

explain: '절망'은 희망이 없는 상태이고, '절망감'은 그걸 마음으로 느끼는 기분이에요. '절망감에 빠지다', '절망감을 느끼다'처럼 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '좌절감'이 있어요.
explain_en: '절망' is the state of having no hope, while '절망감' is the feeling of it inside you. It appears as '절망감에 빠지다' or '절망감을 느끼다', and a similar word is '좌절감'.

examples.ko: 월별 방문자 그래프에 점선으로 평균선을 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please add the average line as a dotted line on the monthly visitors graph.
Please cut the paper along the dotted line.

examples.ko: 점선이 끝나는 곳에 이름을 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please write your name where the dotted line ends.
On the map, the dotted line shows the border.

examples.ko: 점선 부분은 아직 공사 중인 길이에요.
examples.en: The dotted part is a road that is still under construction.
Don't write anything in the dotted box.

explain: 끊기지 않은 '실선'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 서류에서 '점선을 따라 자르세요', '점선 위에 서명하세요'처럼 안내문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It helps to remember it as the pair of '실선', the unbroken line. It often appears in instructions on forms, like '점선을 따라 자르세요' or '점선 위에 서명하세요'.

examples.en: Please take a number ticket first at the reception counter.
I don't know where the reception counter is.

examples.ko: 병원 접수창구 앞에 사람들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: People lined up in front of the hospital reception counter.
You can just hand in the documents at the application counter.
The application counter is open until six in the evening.
The staff at the application counter guided me kindly.

explain: 병원, 구청, 학원처럼 신청하거나 서류를 내는 곳의 창구를 말해요. '접수처'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, '창구'는 직원이 앉아 있는 칸막이 자리를 가리키는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is the counter at places like hospitals, offices and academies where you apply or hand in documents. '접수처' is used similarly, but '창구' more strongly suggests the partitioned spot where a staff member sits.

examples.en: I'm still clumsy with chopsticks.

examples.ko: 저는 젓가락질이 서툴러서 식당에서 포크를 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I'm not good with chopsticks, so I asked for a fork at the restaurant.
My foreign friend learned how to use chopsticks quickly.

examples.ko: 젓가락질 연습을 하려고 콩을 집어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried picking up beans to practice using chopsticks.
Using chopsticks is hard for everyone at first.

examples.ko: 젓가락질 하나만 봐도 밥 먹는 습관이 보여요.
examples.en: You can see someone's eating habits just from how they use chopsticks.

explain: '젓가락'은 도구이고 '젓가락질'은 그걸 쓰는 동작이에요. '젓가락질을 하다', '젓가락질이 서툴다/능숙하다'처럼 말하고, '가위질'처럼 도구 뒤에 '-질'이 붙은 말과 같은 방식이에요.
explain_en: '젓가락' is the tool, and '젓가락질' is the act of using it. You say '젓가락질을 하다' or '젓가락질이 서툴다/능숙하다', and it works like '가위질', where '-질' is attached to a tool.

examples.ko: 김치를 담글 때 젓갈을 넣으면 감칠맛이 나요.
examples.en: Adding jeotgal when making kimchi gives it a rich savory taste.

examples.ko: 할머니가 직접 담근 젓갈이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The jeotgal my grandmother made herself tastes the best.
Jeotgal is salty, so eat just a little.

examples.ko: 젓갈 냄새가 강해서 처음에는 먹기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The smell of jeotgal was strong, so it was hard to eat at first.

examples.ko: 흰밥에 젓갈 하나만 있어도 밥이 잘 넘어가요.
examples.en: Even with just one kind of jeotgal, white rice goes down easily.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구는 젓갈이 들어간 김치를 처음 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: My foreign friend tried kimchi made with jeotgal for the first time.

explain: 새우, 멸치, 명란 같은 해산물을 소금에 절여 삭힌 음식이라서 '새우젓', '멸치젓'처럼 이름 뒤에 '-젓'이 붙기도 해요. 반찬으로 먹기도 하고 김치 양념에도 들어가요.
explain_en: It is seafood such as shrimp, anchovy or pollack roe salted and fermented, so specific kinds often end in '-젓', like '새우젓' and '멸치젓'. It is eaten as a side dish and also goes into kimchi seasoning.

examples.ko: 세 번째 정류소를 지날 때까지 우리는 말없이 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: We sat in silence until we passed the third stop.

examples.ko: 집 앞 정류소에서 오 분만 기다리면 버스가 와요.
examples.en: If you wait just five minutes at the stop in front of my house, a bus comes.
The next stop is our school.
There is a convenience store near the stop, so it's convenient.
Arrival times are shown at every stop.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 정류소 지붕 아래에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: It was raining, so I stood under the roof of the stop.

explain: '정류장'과 같은 곳을 가리켜요. '정류소에서 기다리다', '정류소에서 내리다'처럼 '에서'와 함께 많이 써요. '버스 정류소'처럼 앞에 '버스'를 붙이면 더 분명해요.
explain_en: It refers to the same place as '정류장'. It is often used with '에서', as in '정류소에서 기다리다' or '정류소에서 내리다'. Adding '버스' in front, as in '버스 정류소', makes it clearer.

examples.en: This translator has quite high accuracy.

examples.ko: 일기 예보의 정확도는 예전보다 많이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The accuracy of weather forecasts has improved a lot compared with before.

examples.ko: 정확도를 높이려면 데이터를 더 모아야 해요.
examples.en: To improve accuracy, we need to collect more data.
Speed matters, but accuracy matters more.

examples.ko: 이 앱의 위치 정확도는 몇 미터쯤 될까요?
examples.en: About how many meters is the location accuracy of this app?

examples.ko: 채점 정확도 때문에 답안을 두 번 확인했어요.
examples.en: For the sake of grading accuracy, I checked the answer sheets twice.

explain: '정확성'이 정확한 성질을 말한다면 '정확도'는 얼마나 정확한지 정도를 말해요. 그래서 '정확도가 높다/낮다'처럼 쓰고 번역, 예측, 검색 같은 이야기에 잘 나와요.
explain_en: While '정확성' is the quality of being accurate, '정확도' is the degree of how accurate something is. So you say '정확도가 높다/낮다', and it fits talk about translation, prediction and search.

examples.en: We drew lots to divide the work fairly.
To be fair, we decided the seats by drawing lots.
I drew number one in the lottery draw.
Drawing lots is fair because it's the same no matter who draws.
We shared the year-end party gifts by drawing lots.
The children lined up in the order they drew.

explain: 가위바위보나 사다리타기처럼 운으로 정할 때 쓰는 방법이에요. '제비를 뽑다'라고도 하고, '제비뽑기로 정하다'처럼 방법을 말할 때 '-로'와 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a way to decide by luck, like rock-paper-scissors or ladder drawing. You can also say '제비를 뽑다', and '제비뽑기로 정하다' with '-로' is a common way to state the method.

examples.en: Tomorrow is my grandfather's memorial day, so I'm going to my uncle's house.
On memorial day the family gathers to prepare food.

examples.ko: 제삿날이 다가오면 어머니가 장을 많이 보세요.
examples.en: When the memorial day approaches, my mother does a lot of grocery shopping.
It's a relief that this year's memorial day falls on the weekend.

examples.ko: 제삿날 아침부터 집에서 전 부치는 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: From the morning of the memorial day, the house smelled of pan-fried jeon.
I told the office it was a memorial day and left early.

explain: '제사'는 지내는 일이고 '제삿날'은 그 날짜예요. 같은 날을 '기일'이라고도 하는데, 일상 대화에서는 '제삿날이 다음 주예요'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '제사' is the ritual itself and '제삿날' is the date it is held. The same day is also called '기일', but in everyday talk people often say things like '제삿날이 다음 주예요'.

examples.en: I had jeyukbokkeum near the office for lunch.

examples.ko: 제육볶음은 밥이랑 같이 먹으면 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: Jeyukbokkeum is really delicious with rice.

examples.ko: 상추에 제육볶음을 싸 먹으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes even better when you wrap jeyukbokkeum in lettuce.

examples.ko: 저는 매운 제육볶음이 좋아서 자주 시켜요.
examples.en: I like spicy jeyukbokkeum, so I order it often.
Please pack one jeyukbokkeum lunch box to go.

examples.ko: 어머니가 만든 제육볶음 맛이 아직도 생각나요.
examples.en: I still remember the taste of the jeyukbokkeum my mother made.

explain: 돼지고기를 고추장 양념에 볶은 매콤한 반찬이에요. 식당 메뉴에서는 줄여서 '제육'이라고도 하고, 백반집이나 도시락 메뉴에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a spicy dish of pork stir-fried in a red pepper paste marinade. On restaurant menus it is often shortened to '제육', and you often see it at set-meal restaurants and on lunch box menus.

examples.en: It's the best restaurant in our neighborhood.
He is the top expert in this field.
They say it used to be the wealthiest family of all the rich ones.

examples.ko: 그 집 김치 맛은 이 시장에서 제일간다고 소문났어요.
examples.en: That shop's kimchi is rumored to be the best in this market.

examples.ko: 제일갈 만한 실력이 아니면 뽑히기 어려워요.
examples.en: Unless your skill is among the very best, it's hard to get chosen.
Even the richest person was poor as a child, they say.

explain: '제일가는 + 명사' 모양으로 가장 많이 써요. '제일 좋다'보다 한 범위 안에서 으뜸이라는 느낌이 강해서 '이 동네에서 제일가는 맛집'처럼 범위를 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It is most often used in the form '제일가는 + noun'. Rather than a plain '제일 좋다', it carries the feeling of being at the top within some range, so the range is usually stated, as in '이 동네에서 제일가는 맛집'.

examples.en: The plate fell on the floor and broke into pieces.
The window was hit by a ball and shattered.
Please be careful when throwing away the broken cup.
The plan I prepared for so long fell apart in an instant.

examples.ko: 얼음이 조각나서 호수 위를 건널 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The ice broke into pieces, so we couldn't cross the lake.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 화면이 조각날 정도로 세게 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The phone fell so hard that the screen almost shattered.

explain: 접시나 유리 같은 물건이 여러 조각으로 깨질 때 쓰고, 계획이나 꿈이 무너질 때처럼 비유로도 써요. '산산조각 나다'라고 하면 훨씬 세게 부서진 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when things like plates or glass break into several pieces, and also figuratively when plans or dreams collapse. '산산조각 나다' sounds like it broke much more violently.

examples.en: I looked at old sculptures at the museum.

examples.ko: 공원 한가운데에 큰 조각품이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A large sculpture stands in the middle of the park.
They say this sculpture was made from a single piece of wood.

examples.ko: 친구가 여행 기념으로 작은 조각품을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: My friend bought a small sculpture as a souvenir of the trip.
Is it okay to take photos in front of the sculpture?
Do you want to go to the sculpture exhibition together?

explain: '조각'이 만드는 일이나 예술 분야를 말한다면 '조각품'은 완성된 작품이에요. 사람이나 동물 모양이면 '조각상'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: While '조각' can refer to the act or the art field of carving, '조각품' is the finished work. If it takes the shape of a person or animal, it is also called '조각상'.

examples.en: In the old days, rice or shells were used like money.
I picked up pretty shells at the beach.

examples.ko: 조개껍데기에 귀를 대면 파도 소리가 나는 것 같아요.
examples.en: If you hold a shell to your ear, it sounds like waves.
The child made a necklace out of shells.

examples.ko: 조개껍데기 안에 작은 게가 숨어 있었어요.
examples.en: A small crab was hiding inside the shell.

examples.ko: 모래 위에 조개껍데기가 여기저기 흩어져 있어요.
examples.en: Shells are scattered here and there on the sand.

explain: '껍데기'는 조개나 달걀처럼 딱딱한 겉을 말하고, 과일이나 양파처럼 벗겨 내는 부드러운 겉은 보통 '껍질'이라고 해요. 조개는 '조개껍질'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '껍데기' is for hard outsides such as shellfish or eggs, while the softer peel of fruit or onions is usually called '껍질'. A shell is also called '조개껍질'.

examples.ko: 골목이 너무 좁다래서 차가 못 들어가요.
examples.en: The alley is so narrow that cars can't get in.

examples.ko: 좁다란 길을 따라 걸으니 작은 가게가 나왔어요.
examples.en: Walking along the narrow path, a small shop appeared.
The room is narrow, but it's fine for living alone.
The hallway continues on, narrow.
That house has a yard that is narrow and long.
The kitchen in this house is really cramped.

explain: '좁다'보다 길쭉하고 폭이 아주 좁아서 답답한 느낌이 강해요. 'ㅎ'이 빠지는 불규칙 활용이라 '좁다래요', '좁다란'처럼 바뀌어요.
explain_en: Compared with '좁다', it has a stronger feel of being long and very narrow, making things feel cramped. It is an irregular 'ㅎ' verb that changes to forms like '좁다래요' and '좁다란'.

examples.en: Separating trash by type is important.
Bookstores arrange books by category.
I sorted the clothes by type and put them in the drawers.

examples.ko: 종류별 가격이 다르니까 꼼꼼히 비교해 보세요.
examples.en: Prices differ by type, so compare carefully.
At the mart, instant noodles are stacked by type.

examples.ko: 자료를 종류별로 모아서 파일로 만들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please gather the materials by type and make them into a file.

explain: '종류'에 '-별'이 붙어서 '종류에 따라 나눈다'는 느낌을 줘요. '나이별', '지역별'처럼 '-별'은 앞말에 붙여 쓰고, '종류별로'처럼 '-로'를 붙이는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '-별' is added to '종류' to give the feel of dividing according to type. Like '나이별' and '지역별', '-별' is written attached to the word before it, and '-로' is often added, as in '종류별로'.

examples.en: In the UK cars drive on the left, so I was confused at first.
It says that this path is left-side traffic.

examples.ko: 옛날 학교 복도에는 좌측통행 표시가 있었어요.
examples.en: The old school hallways had left-side walking signs.
First check whether it's left-side or right-side traffic.

examples.ko: 공사 중이라 이 구간은 좌측통행으로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: Because of construction, this section changed to left-side traffic.

examples.ko: 좌측통행을 모르는 관광객이 많아서 안내판을 붙였어요.
examples.en: Many tourists didn't know about left-side traffic, so they put up a sign.

explain: 반대말은 '우측통행'이에요. 영국이나 일본처럼 차가 왼쪽으로 다니는 나라도 있어서, 길이나 도로 이야기에서 어느 쪽인지 확인할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '우측통행'. Some countries, such as the UK and Japan, have cars driving on the left, so it often comes up when checking which side to use on roads and paths.

examples.en: Today I came wearing a black pleated skirt.
A pleated skirt sways prettily when the wind blows.

examples.ko: 교복 주름치마가 너무 짧아서 길이를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: My uniform pleated skirt was too short, so I lengthened it.
I'm looking for a blouse that goes with a pleated skirt.

examples.ko: 주름치마 주름이 풀리지 않게 조심해서 빨아 주세요.
examples.en: Please wash the pleated skirt carefully so the pleats don't come undone.

examples.ko: 언니가 물려준 주름치마가 아직도 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: The pleated skirt my sister handed down still fits well.

explain: '플리츠 스커트'와 같은 옷이에요. 옷 가게에서는 외래어도 들을 수 있지만, 일상 대화에서는 '주름치마'라고 해도 다 통해요.
explain_en: It is the same garment as a '플리츠 스커트' (pleated skirt). You may hear the loanword in clothing shops, but '주름치마' is understood in everyday talk.

examples.en: The main purpose of this trip is to rest.
What is the main purpose of this meeting?

examples.ko: 돈 버는 것이 제 주목적은 아니에요.
examples.en: Making money is not my main goal.
Don't forget the main objective when you make the plan.

examples.ko: 주목적과 부수적인 목적을 나눠서 적어 보세요.
examples.en: Try writing down the main objective separately from the side objectives.
My main reason for coming to Korea is to study abroad.

explain: '목적' 앞에 '주'가 붙어서 여러 목적 중 가장 중요한 것을 가리켜요. '주목적은 ~예요'처럼 문장 속에서 쓰이고, 짝이 되는 말로는 '부수적인 목적'이 있어요.
explain_en: With '주' in front of '목적', it points to the most important among several purposes. It is used in sentences like '주목적은 ~예요', and its counterpart is '부수적인 목적' (a side purpose).

examples.ko: 주요리는 소고기와 생선 중에서 고를 수 있어요.
examples.en: For the main dish, you can choose between beef and fish.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 주요리보다 후식이 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: At this restaurant the dessert is tastier than the main dish.

examples.ko: 주요리가 나오기 전에 샐러드를 먼저 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate a salad first before the main dish came out.
I prepared a chicken dish as the main course.

examples.ko: 주요리 양이 많아서 사이드는 하나만 시켰어요.
examples.en: The main dish was big, so I ordered only one side.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁 주요리는 제가 직접 만들게요.
examples.en: I'll make tonight's main dish myself.

explain: '메인 요리'라고도 해요. 코스 요리에서는 앞에 나오는 '전채', 뒤에 나오는 '후식'과 순서로 같이 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is also called '메인 요리'. In a course meal, it is easy to remember in order with the starter '전채' before it and the dessert '후식' after it.

examples.ko: 창밖에 황혼이 내려앉자 방 안이 주홍빛으로 물들었어요.
examples.en: When dusk settled outside the window, the room was tinged scarlet.
I walked along the beach watching the scarlet sunset.

examples.ko: 가을이 되자 산이 주홍빛 단풍으로 가득해요.
examples.en: With autumn, the mountain is full of scarlet maple leaves.

examples.ko: 촛불이 주홍빛을 내며 천천히 타고 있었어요.
examples.en: The candle was burning slowly, giving off a scarlet glow.

examples.ko: 그녀의 볼이 주홍빛이 될 만큼 부끄러웠어요.
examples.en: She was so embarrassed that her cheeks turned scarlet.

examples.ko: 주홍빛 감이 나무마다 주렁주렁 달려 있어요.
examples.en: Scarlet persimmons hang in bunches on every tree.

explain: '주홍색'이 색 이름이라면 '주홍빛'은 노을, 불빛, 단풍처럼 그런 색으로 보이는 기운에 더 잘 어울려요. '주황'보다 빨간 쪽에 가까운 색이에요.
explain_en: If '주홍색' is the name of the color, '주홍빛' suits the tint things appear to have, like a sunset, firelight or autumn leaves. The color is closer to red than '주황' is.

examples.ko: 주홍색 스카프를 하니까 얼굴이 환해 보여요.
examples.en: With the scarlet scarf on, your face looks bright.
That traffic light looks close to scarlet.

examples.ko: 미술 시간에 주홍색 물감을 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: I used a lot of scarlet paint in art class.
Scarlet looks a bit softer than red.
After painting the wall scarlet, the atmosphere became warm.

examples.ko: 저는 주홍색과 주황색을 잘 구분하지 못해요.
examples.en: I can't tell scarlet and orange apart very well.

explain: '주황색'이 오렌지색이라면 '주홍색'은 거기에 붉은 기가 더 도는 색이에요. 둘이 헷갈리니까 옷이나 물감 색을 말할 때는 사진을 같이 보여 주면 편해요.
explain_en: If '주황색' is orange, '주홍색' has more red in it. The two are easy to mix up, so when talking about clothes or paint colors it helps to show a picture too.

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 하늘이 주황빛으로 물들어요.
examples.en: When the sun sets, the sky is tinged orange.
I waited for my friend under an orange street lamp.
The tangerines ripened and their orange color became vivid.

examples.ko: 난로 속 불꽃이 주황빛을 띠고 있어요.
examples.en: The flame inside the stove has an orange tint.

examples.ko: 주황빛은 보기만 해도 따뜻한 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: Just looking at orange gives a warm feeling.

examples.ko: 저녁 노을이 바다 위에 주황빛 길을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The evening glow made an orange path over the sea.

explain: '주황색'이 색 이름이라면 '주황빛'은 노을이나 불빛에서 느껴지는 오렌지색 기운에 어울려요. '주홍빛'보다는 덜 붉고 귤색에 가까워요.
explain_en: If '주황색' is the color name, '주황빛' suits the orange tint you feel in a sunset or a light. It is less red than '주홍빛' and closer to the color of a tangerine.

examples.ko: 동생은 준비성이 좋아서 늘 우산을 들고 다녀요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is well-prepared and always carries an umbrella.

examples.ko: 준비성이 철저한 친구 덕분에 여행이 편했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my thorough, well-prepared friend, the trip was easy.

examples.ko: 준비성 없이 나왔다가 비를 홀딱 맞았어요.
examples.en: I came out unprepared and got completely soaked in the rain.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 준비성이 부족해서 항상 마지막에 서둘러요.
examples.en: He lacks preparedness, so he always rushes at the end.
Everyone was amazed at our team leader's preparedness.
Preparedness starts from small habits.

explain: '준비'는 하는 일이고 '준비성'은 미리 챙기는 성격이에요. '준비성이 있다/없다/철저하다'처럼 사람의 성격을 말할 때 쓰고, '-성'이 성질을 나타내는 말이에요.
explain_en: '준비' is the act of preparing, while '준비성' is the trait of getting ready ahead of time. It is used for a person's character, as in '준비성이 있다/없다/철저하다', where '-성' marks a quality.

examples.en: The final exam has more questions than the midterm.
The midterm exams start next week.
Because of midterms, I practically live in the library these days.
My math score went up a lot on the midterm.
The teacher said the midterm wouldn't be hard.

examples.ko: 중간시험을 망쳐서 기말시험에 더 열심히 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: I messed up the midterm, so I decided to work harder for the final.

explain: 학교에서는 '중간고사'라고도 많이 말해요. 짝이 되는 말은 학기 끝에 보는 '기말시험'(기말고사)이에요.
explain_en: At school people also often say '중간고사'. Its counterpart is '기말시험' (기말고사), the exam taken at the end of the term.

examples.ko: 이 책은 중고생을 위해 쉽게 쓴 책이에요.
examples.en: This book was written in an easy way for middle and high school students.

examples.ko: 중고생은 방학 때도 학원에 다니는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Middle and high school students often attend academies even during vacation.

examples.ko: 요즘 중고생 사이에서 이 노래가 인기예요.
examples.en: This song is popular among middle and high schoolers these days.
I asked whether there is a discount for middle and high school students.

examples.ko: 저는 중고생 때 매일 아침 일찍 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: When I was in middle and high school, I went to school early every morning.

examples.ko: 버스 안에 교복 입은 중고생들이 가득해요.
examples.en: The bus is full of middle and high schoolers in uniforms.

explain: '중학생'과 '고등학생'을 함께 부르는 말이에요. 같은 방식으로 초등학생까지 묶으면 '초중고생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a word for middle school and high school students together. In the same way, adding elementary students gives '초중고생'.

examples.ko: 중고품 가게에서 안 쓰는 물건을 사 줘요.
examples.en: The secondhand shop buys items you no longer use.

examples.ko: 중고품은 값이 싸지만 상태를 꼭 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: Secondhand items are cheap, but you must check their condition.
I buy and sell secondhand items through an app.
This desk is secondhand, but it's as clean as new.

examples.ko: 중고품 거래할 때는 직접 만나서 확인하세요.
examples.en: When trading secondhand items, meet in person to check.
I sold the furniture I wasn't using as secondhand goods.

explain: '중고차', '중고책'처럼 '중고'는 이미 한 번 쓴 물건을 뜻하고, 반대는 '새 제품'이에요. '중고'가 중학교·고등학교의 '중고'와 소리가 같으니 문장 속에서 구별하세요.
explain_en: As in '중고차' and '중고책', '중고' means something that has already been used once, and the opposite is '새 제품'. It sounds the same as the '중고' in middle and high school, so tell them apart by context.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 학기에 한국어 중급반에서 공부해요.
examples.en: I'm studying in the Korean intermediate class this term.
To move up to the intermediate class, you have to take a test.
The intermediate swimming class learns freestyle and backstroke.
The intermediate class meets every Tuesday and Thursday.
I went to the application counter to sign up for the intermediate class.
My older sister registered for the intermediate yoga class.

explain: '초급반', '고급반'과 같이 단계를 나눈 반 이름이에요. 한국어 학원이나 운동 수업에서 레벨 테스트 후에 '중급반에 들어가다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a class name used in a leveled series with '초급반' and '고급반'. At Korean language schools or exercise classes you say things like '중급반에 들어가다' after a level test.

examples.en: My parents had an arranged marriage.

examples.ko: 중매결혼이라도 서로 사랑하며 사는 부부가 많아요.
examples.en: Even if it was an arranged marriage, many couples live lovingly together.
They say Grandma met Grandpa through an arranged marriage.

examples.ko: 연애결혼과 중매결혼 중에 뭐가 더 좋다고 생각해요?
examples.en: Which do you think is better, a love marriage or an arranged marriage?
I was curious how arranged marriages work, so I asked.
When the topic of arranged marriage came up, my mother smiled.

explain: '연애결혼'의 반대로 기억하면 좋아요. 중매는 사람을 소개해 주는 일이라서 '중매로 결혼했어요'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It helps to remember it as the opposite of '연애결혼' (a love marriage). Matchmaking is introducing people to each other, so you can also say '중매로 결혼했어요'.

examples.en: This novel has three central characters.

examples.ko: 그는 이번 일의 중심인물로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: He is known as the central figure in this matter.
The central member left suddenly and the group wavered.
Try following the central character's feelings in the movie.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 사건의 중심인물을 정리해 보세요.
examples.en: Before the presentation, try organizing the central figures of the case.
I took on the role of the central figure at the village event.

explain: '주인공'은 이야기의 가장 중요한 사람이고, '중심인물'은 소설뿐 아니라 사건이나 모임에서 일이 그 사람을 중심으로 돌아갈 때도 써요. 뉴스나 수업에서는 '사건의 중심인물'처럼 나와요.
explain_en: '주인공' is the most important person in a story, while '중심인물' can also be used for events or groups when things revolve around that person. In news and lessons it appears as '사건의 중심인물'.

examples.en: My father likes to wear gray suits.

examples.ko: 쥐색 코트가 어두운 옷에도 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: A gray coat also goes well with dark clothes.

examples.ko: 벽을 쥐색으로 칠했더니 차분한 느낌이 나요.
examples.en: After painting the wall gray, it feels calm.

examples.ko: 쥐색은 때가 잘 안 타서 좋아요.
examples.en: Gray is nice because it doesn't show dirt easily.
Gray clouds rolled in, so I grabbed an umbrella.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 검은색 말고 쥐색도 있어요.
examples.en: This bag comes in gray as well as black.

explain: '회색'보다 어두운 쪽을 가리킬 때 써요. 양복, 코트, 가구 색을 말할 때 자주 들어요. 더 밝은 회색은 '연회색'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It points to a darker gray than plain '회색'. You often hear it for the color of suits, coats and furniture. A lighter gray is called '연회색'.

examples.ko: 영화 볼 때 쥐포를 구워 먹었어요.
examples.en: I grilled and ate dried filefish while watching a movie.

examples.ko: 쥐포는 불에 구우면 고소한 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: Dried filefish gives off a savory smell when grilled over a fire.
I bought a bag of dried filefish at the market.

examples.ko: 쥐포가 너무 딱딱해서 잘게 찢어 먹었어요.
examples.en: The dried filefish was too hard, so I tore it into small pieces to eat.

examples.ko: 동생은 쥐포에 마요네즈를 찍어 먹는 걸 좋아해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling likes dipping dried filefish in mayonnaise.
The smell of grilling dried filefish spread all the way down the alley.

explain: 쥐치라는 생선을 납작하게 말려 만든 간식이에요. 보통 불에 살짝 구워서 찢어 먹고, 마요네즈나 고추장에 찍어 먹기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a snack made by drying filefish (쥐치) into a flat sheet. It is usually lightly grilled and torn into strips, and some people dip it in mayonnaise or red pepper paste.

examples.en: The children are playing happily in the yard.
Please welcome the arriving guests cheerfully.
Everyone walked along, singing happily.
He did even hard work gladly.
I hope you spend this holiday joyfully.
Grandfather listened to his grandchildren's stories with delight.

explain: '즐겁게'로 바꿔 써도 뜻은 같아요. 말할 때는 '즐겁게'가 자연스럽고, '즐거이'는 글이나 인사말에서 조금 점잖은 느낌으로 쓰여요.
explain_en: You can swap it with '즐겁게' without changing the meaning. In speech '즐겁게' sounds natural, while '즐거이' has a slightly refined feel in writing and greetings.

examples.en: My great-grandmother turned ninety this year.
On the holidays I bow to my great-grandmother.
My great-grandmother's house is near the sea.
My great-grandmother told me stories from her childhood.
My great-grandmother is in our family photo too.

examples.ko: 저는 증조할머니를 한 번밖에 못 만났어요.
examples.en: I could only meet my great-grandmother once.

explain: '증조할아버지'와 짝이에요. 어머니 쪽 증조할머니는 '외증조할머니'라고 구분하기도 해요. 높임 말이라서 '있어요' 대신 '계세요', '이/가' 대신 '께서', '에게' 대신 '께'를 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with '증조할아버지'. A great-grandmother on your mother's side is sometimes distinguished as '외증조할머니'. It is an honorific word, so use '계세요' instead of '있어요', '께서' instead of '이/가', and '께' instead of '에게'.
